title: Help
subtitle: What you can do in Lab Console, and what to do when something is stuck

sections.title: The sections of Lab Console
sections.intro: The left-hand bar leads to every section. Your badge, at the bottom, opens your account menu.
sections.home: Home: where you land after signing in: your team, its bench, your latest backups, the bench's activity, your next slots.
sections.consoles: Consoles: pick a bench, then click a device on the diagram to open its console. This is where you take the bench for your team, type your commands and see who is working on what ("Live", "Bench wall").
sections.overview: Overview: every bench of the lab at a glance, one card per bench.
sections.team: Team: create the team of your lab group, invite your classmates, answer an invitation, book a bench in the calendar.
sections.jobs: Backups: back up the configuration of every device of a bench, compare it, inject it again, or reset the bench. Your backups and the lab templates are here too.
sections.infra: Infra: the Proxmox VMs when Proxmox is configured, and the admin switches of the lab.
sections.status: Lab status: whether the access chain answers (jump server, console servers), and what is recorded.
sections.admin: Admin (administrators only): accounts, invitations, SSO sign-in, lab parameters, diagram, sessions, audit trail, announcement.
sections.account: My account (from your badge): display name, password and passkeys of a local account, open sessions.
sections.help: Help: this page. The account menu also lets you replay the guided tour.
sections.extras: Also in the left-hand bar: FR / EN switches the language, "Theme" switches light and dark, and the "Alerts" bell turns on browser alerts (keyboard asked for, line free, job finished).

home.title: Home and overview
home.intro: These two pages only show, and keep themselves up to date. Taking, joining or releasing a bench is still done in the bench bar, in the Consoles section.
home.homeTeam: Home: your team and its members, the invitations waiting for you, your team's bench (or the one you are a guest of), your next slots, the lab in numbers and the current announcement.
home.homeBackups: Your team's five latest backups: only its members see them, not a guest, not another team.
home.homeActivity: The activity of your bench since your team took it: who took, joined or left it, the jobs started, the consoles opened. Only the bench's occupants see it.
home.homeNone: With no team, or if your team has no bench, Home tells you what to do and leads you to the right section.
home.overview: Overview: for each bench, the team holding it and since when, who is on it (guests are marked), the open consoles and who has the keyboard, the running job, the lock and its reason, the next three slots and the automatic release time.
home.overviewLines: A card's lines: open in Lab Console, busy outside Lab Console, silent; and, for half an hour after a "Line status" check, the lines found free and when it ran.
home.overviewFilter: The filter shows every bench, the free ones or yours. A card leads to the bench (Consoles section) and to its backups.
home.overviewPrivate: The overview never shows a team's backups or journal, nor what was typed on a console.

team.title: Taking a bench with your team
team.intro: Benches belong to a team, not to a person. You are in one team at a time.
team.step1: Team section, "My team" tab: "Create the team", then invite your classmates by their sign-in name. A classmate who signs in through the university is only known after their first sign-in.
team.step2: Each person invited answers in the Team section: "Join" or "Decline".
team.step3: Consoles section: pick the bench, then "Take the bench". Every member of the team becomes an occupant.
team.step4: When you leave: "Release the bench". Back up first (see below).
team.idle: A bench with no activity at all for {hours} h is released automatically. "We are still here" keeps it yours.
team.idleUnknown: A bench with no activity for a while is released automatically. "We are still here" keeps it yours.
team.taken: On a bench taken by another team you can watch the consoles that are already open but not type. "Ask to join" sends a request: a member of the team accepts or refuses. An accepted guest is an occupant until they leave the bench or it is released.
team.free: On a free bench anyone can open a console. Take the bench anyway: without it your backups and jobs have no team to belong to.
team.reserve: Team section, "Bookings" tab: book a slot for your team. When the slot starts you can take the bench; its current occupants are warned ten minutes before.
team.lock: An administrator can lock a bench (a graded lab, for instance): the reason is shown, and nobody but administrators opens a console or starts a job on it.
team.history: The bench's "History": who took, backed up, injected or reset it, and when.
team.group: "Notes & chat" opens beside the diagram the note of each device (everyone reads it, occupants edit it) and the bench chat (occupants only, 500 characters per message). They stay with the team.

share.title: Sharing a console and asking for the keyboard
share.intro: A console exists once: if a classmate has already opened the device, you join the same console and see what it displayed recently. One person at a time holds the keyboard, the others watch.
share.who: Anyone can watch an open console. Typing needs the right to drive the device: being an occupant of its bench (or an administrator), or the bench being free. Otherwise the console says "You may watch, not type."
share.ask: To type while someone else holds the keyboard: "Ask for the keyboard". The pilot sees the request and answers "Give the keyboard" or "Refuse". With no answer after 30 seconds the keyboard comes to you; it comes at once if the pilot has typed nothing for 2 minutes.
share.give: If you hold it: "Give the keyboard back" frees it. "Share the keyboard" lets everyone who may drive the device type; "Take the keyboard back" gives it back to you alone.
share.admin: An administrator can take the keyboard outright.
share.task: While a job runs on a console (export, injection, backup…) its keyboard is suspended until the end. "Stop" interrupts the job.
share.free: "Free the line" closes the console for everyone and gives the line back to the console server. Without it, the line stays open while someone is watching, for 30 seconds after the last person leaves, and closes by itself after a long time without typing.
share.live: "Live" lists the open consoles, who is on them and the last command typed. "Bench wall" shows every open console of a bench, read-only. "Find a device" (Ctrl K, in the Consoles section) opens a device by its name, bench or port.
share.tools: Each console has its tools: send a BREAK, export the running-config as .txt, inject a script, send the same commands to several consoles, search its history, write the device's note. Pasting several lines sends them one by one (you need the keyboard).

backup.title: Backing up: the server is not a backup
backup.warning: The server is not a backup: it may be wiped between two sessions. After every backup, download the ZIP and keep it yourself.
backup.step1: Backups section: pick the bench, then "Back up".
backup.step2: Tick the devices and name the backup ("Lab 3 end of session"). If a device asks for an enable password, type it: it is used during the job only, never stored or logged.
backup.step3: Each device's running-config is read (and the VLANs of a switch) and filed in a backup of your team.
backup.step4: "Download the ZIP" right away, not later.
backup.offer: When you release the bench by hand, the application offers to back it up. The offer lasts 30 minutes; you find it again in the Backups section.
backup.list: "Team backups": view a configuration, its ZIP, "Differences…" between two backups, "Compare with live", "Inject", "Lab folder" (configurations and console journals), "Delete", "Import a ZIP", and a search across every configuration.
backup.owner: Backups belong to the team that held the bench: its members and the administrators see them.
backup.templates: "Lab templates": starting configurations published by administrators, which you can inject on your bench.
backup.cisco: Only Cisco IOS and IOS XE devices are backed up; any other system is recognised and left untouched.
backup.single: For a single device, the "Export config" button of its console downloads its show running-config as a .txt file.

tasks.title: Injection and reset, and their safeguards
tasks.intro: These are jobs: they run on the server, take the keyboard of the bench's consoles, everyone follows them live and they can be stopped. One job at a time per bench. Only the occupants of the bench and administrators start one, and a locked bench accepts none. A job only touches Cisco IOS or IOS XE.
tasks.inject1: Pick a backup or a lab template, then "Preview": you read the exact script each device will receive before anything starts.
tasks.inject2: Mode "Reset, then inject (recommended)" or "Merge with the current configuration". Every device is backed up first; in merge mode a device whose backup fails is refused.
tasks.inject3: Some lines of a running-config cannot be replayed (licences, certificates, factory values): they are removed and the preview counts them.
tasks.inject4: Then the device is read again and compared with the source. "Save afterwards (copy run start)" only happens if everything was accepted; otherwise the report shows the refused lines.
tasks.reset1: The dialog lists the devices, the people connected to them and what will be erased: the startup-config, flash:vlan.dat on a switch (all VLANs), the configuration register put back to 0x2102 on a router, then a reload without saving.
tasks.reset2: For each device the configuration is backed up first and read back. If the backup fails the device is not erased (only an administrator can force it).
tasks.reset3: You must type the bench's name to confirm. A countdown of a few seconds then leaves time to stop: nothing is typed while it runs.
tasks.reset4: A device that shares its console line with another bench is unticked by default, and refused if that other bench is held by another team or locked.
tasks.reset5: The reload takes several minutes depending on the model. The job goes on in the server if you close the page; its report (device by device, refused lines included) is in "Recent jobs of the bench".
tasks.stop: In every case "Stop" is available to the person who started the job, to the bench's occupants and to administrators.

checks.title: Checking the bench
checks.intro: The "Checks" button, at the top of the Consoles section, opens the checks of the bench you picked. They only read: show commands and pings, nothing is configured. People watching a console see the check go by.
checks.lines: Line status: for each device, is the line free, busy outside Lab Console, already open in Lab Console, or is the device silent? The result is shown on the diagram for half an hour and on the bench's card in the overview; everyone sees it.
checks.cabling: Cabling (CDP): show cdp neighbors detail on every device, compared with the diagram's links: as drawn, on another port, missing (with the reason: interface shut down, down, no such port), cannot be checked, or a cable nobody drew. The verdict is shown on the diagram's links too.
checks.ping: Ping matrix: the routers' addresses are read from their active interfaces, then each router pings the addresses of the others. Green: answers; orange: partly; red: no answer.
checks.interfaces: Addresses and interfaces: show ip interface brief on every device; the address and state of each end of a link are written next to the diagram's links.
checks.who: Only the bench's occupants (and administrators) run a check. One at a time per bench, never during a job (backup, injection, reset); and while a check runs, neither a job nor a password recovery starts on the bench.
checks.untouched: A console open in Lab Console, or busy outside Lab Console, is never touched: the device is skipped and nothing is typed on it, not even Enter. A device waiting for an answer (ROMMON, initial dialog, [confirm]) or not running Cisco IOS is skipped too.
checks.results: The last result of each check stays on screen, even after the page is reloaded. The line status is for everyone; the cabling, pings and addresses for the team that held the bench, the person who ran the check and administrators.
checks.stop: "Stop" interrupts a check: the person who started it, the bench's occupants and administrators can.
checks.limits: The line status can only be run again after a short while, and everyone is limited to a few checks a minute.

recovery.title: Lost password: recovery
recovery.intro: For a device locked by a console password or an enable secret nobody knows. Someone must be in front of the device to power it off and on when the assistant asks.
recovery.step1: Open the device's console, click "Password recovery" on its tile, pick the device's family, then "Start the recovery".
recovery.step2: The assistant first reads the console, then says what to do at each step. Only the person who started it confirms the steps ("Do this step").
recovery.step3: When told, the person on site powers the device off and on (holding the Mode button on a switch); the assistant goes through ROMMON or switch: and boots the device without its startup-config.
recovery.step4: The device reaches its factory prompt (Router>, Switch>), with the factory configuration.
recovery.kept: The startup-config is neither erased nor changed, only ignored for that boot: the assistant makes the next boot read it again. It still holds the old passwords: inject a backup and save it, or reset the device, from the Backups section, or it will be locked again at its next reload.
recovery.notLocked: A device already at a privileged prompt is not locked: the assistant stops without typing anything.
recovery.stop: Stopped, abandoned (nobody confirms) or failed: the assistant first puts the device back as it found it. If it cannot, it says so, and starting the assistant again finishes putting it back.
recovery.who: The bench's occupants and administrators start a recovery; one at a time per device, never during a job or a check of the bench. The diagram marks the device being recovered, and the bench's occupants can follow it.
recovery.close: Closing the window does not stop the recovery: it goes on on the server, and opening the assistant again finds it where it is.
recovery.families: Families: 1841, 2801, 2811 and ISR 4331 routers; 2960, 3560, Catalyst 1000 and 9300L switches. The assistant says when a procedure has not been tried on the real equipment yet.
recovery.disabled: A switch where recovery was disabled (no service password-recovery) offers to erase its configuration: the assistant always answers no, and the switch boots normally.

journal.title: What is recorded, and for how long
journal.intro: What you do here is not anonymous. The up-to-date detail is in Lab status, "What is recorded" tab.
journal.consoles: Console journal: what the devices print, with who held the keyboard. Kept {days} days. No keystroke is recorded as such, but what the device echoes back, so your commands, is in it; a password typed without echo never is. It is readable for a console's whole day: by those who were on it with the right to drive it (only watching does not count), by the team that held the bench that day and by administrators. The "Journals" button downloads it.
journal.consolesUnknown: Console journal: what the devices print, with who held the keyboard, kept for a limited number of days. No keystroke is recorded as such, but what the device echoes back, so your commands, is in it; a password typed without echo never is. It is readable for a console's whole day: by those who were on it with the right to drive it (only watching does not count), by the team that held the bench that day and by administrators. The "Journals" button downloads it.
journal.jobs: What jobs read or send (configurations) does not enter the console journal: a simple marker takes its place.
journal.audit: Audit trail: sign-ins, console openings, keyboard hand-overs, team and bench actions, backups, injections and resets, administration actions, with the person and the time. Administrators read it, with no automatic deletion. A bench's "History" shows its occupants the essentials.
journal.kept: Backups, device notes and chats stay on the server until someone deletes them. The chat keeps the last 200 messages per bench and team, and goes away with the team. Remember: the server is not a backup.
journal.session: Your session ends after {idle} h without activity, and after {max} h at the latest.
journal.never: Never kept: your passwords (only a fingerprint), one-time codes, what you type without echo in the consoles (a password). Commands the device echoes back do appear in the console journal.

trouble.title: When something is stuck
trouble.busy: On the diagram the device is marked "Busy outside Lab Console": the console server refuses the line because someone is connected to it outside Lab Console (another terminal, for instance), or because it is out of service. Click "Tell me when it is free": the line is watched for 30 minutes at most and you are told. Turn on the "Alerts" bell to be told when the window is hidden too. If nothing changes, talk to the instructor.
trouble.busy2: To see the whole bench at once: "Checks", then "Line status", tells which lines are free, busy or silent.
trouble.silent: "Device silent": the console server opened the line but nothing comes back after Enter. It is not Lab Console: check on site that the device is powered on and that its console cable is plugged in.
trouble.lockedTitle: The device asks for a password
trouble.locked: If the console shows "Password:" before you typed anything, a previous group left a password on the console line. Lab Console does not know it and does not bypass it: ask the previous group or the instructor. Jobs (backup, injection, reset) never force a device they cannot bring to privileged mode: it is flagged in the report and left as it is.
trouble.locked2: If nobody knows the password, the "Password recovery" assistant of the console tile bypasses it, with someone on site to power the device off and on (see "Lost password: recovery").
trouble.dialogTitle: The device offers the initial configuration
trouble.dialog: A device with no configuration asks "Would you like to enter the initial configuration dialog?": answer no. Jobs do it by themselves.
trouble.watch: "You may watch, not type": ask for the keyboard if a classmate has it; if the bench is held by another team, ask to join it; if a job is running on the console, wait for it to end.
trouble.lost: "Disconnected" or "Connection to the platform was lost": "Reconnect". A console also closes after a long time without typing, and the line is then free for others.

keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keys.intro: No shortcut takes a terminal's keys: Ctrl C stays the device's interrupt, and Ctrl K there erases to the end of the line as on Cisco.

finder.what: Find a device (in the Consoles section, outside a terminal).

finderMove.what: In the finder: choose a device and open its console. Esc closes.

device.what: On the diagram: move from device to device and open its console.

copy.what: Copy the selected text in a terminal.

send.what: Send, in the script injection dialog and in the one that sends to several consoles.

chat.what: Send a message in the bench chat.

close.what: Close a dialog or the account menu.

splitter.what: On the bar between the diagram and the consoles: move it.

home.title: Your home page
home.body: This is where you land after signing in: your team, the bench it took, your latest backups and what happened on the bench. “Overview”, in the bar on the left, shows every bench of the lab.

bench.title: Pick a bench
bench.body: The lab is split into benches of routers and switches. Click a bench's name, then a device on the diagram to open its console.

team.title: Take the bench with your team
team.body: A bench is taken for the team. Create or join yours in the Team section, then click "Take the bench" in this bar: your classmates become occupants with you.

console.title: Open a console
console.body: Click a device on the diagram: its console opens in your workspace. If a classmate already opened it, you join it and see what it displayed.

keyboard.title: Ask for the keyboard
keyboard.body: One person types at a time: whoever holds the keyboard. If a classmate has it, "Ask for the keyboard" above the console lets them know; with no answer in 30 seconds it comes to you.

backup.title: Back up before you leave
backup.body: In Backups, "Back up" reads the configuration of every device of the bench. The server is not a backup: download the ZIP afterwards. The Help section covers the rest; your account menu lets you replay this tour.
